The important point is that these great signs are not all the signs, but they are among God's signs, some of His signs.

﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ﴾ ("Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful"): ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾, the referent of "that" is what was mentioned about the running of the ships in the sea by God's blessings, and what is witnessed in the sea of God's signs.
﴿لَآيَاتٍ﴾ means: indeed, many signs. The word (آيات) here is the postponed subject of (إنَّ), and ﴿فِي ذَلِكَ﴾ is a prepositional phrase serving as its predicate, placed first.

The author says: (﴿لَآيَاتٍ﴾ lessons, by which a person takes heed and infers the perfection of God's power, glorified and exalted).
(﴿لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ﴾ against the disobedience of God, ﴿شَكُورٍ﴾ for His blessings). (صَبَّار) is an intensive form: one who is very patient. (شكور) is also an intensive form: one who is very thankful.

As for His words ﴿لَآيَاتٍ لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ﴾, what is the connection between mentioning the patient and grateful person after mentioning that the ships run in the sea by God's blessing? The connection is very clear: these ships that run in the sea are sometimes battered by waves, and a person is harmed by that and may suffer damage, so what meets that? Patience. And sometimes the reverse happens: crossing the sea becomes easy and much good results, so that is met with gratitude. Since these ships contain both ease and hardship, God concluded the verse with His words: ﴿لَآيَاتٍ لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ﴾.

Accordingly, we say: in the author's words (﴿لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ﴾ against the disobedience of God) there is some deficiency. Rather, we say: for everyone patient in refraining from His disobedience and in the face of His painful decrees, and grateful for what? For His blessings, as the author said.

(﴿وَإِذَا غَشِيَهُمْ﴾, that is: a wave overspread the disbelievers ﴿مَوْجٌ كَالظُّلَلِ﴾ [Luqman 32], like mountains that shade those beneath them.)

﴿غَشِيَهُمْ﴾: the author says (that is: overspread the disbelievers). The original meaning of (التغشية) is covering, as in His words: ﴿إِذْ يُغَشِّيكُمُ النُّعَاسَ أَمَنَةً﴾ [al-Anfal 11], and His words: ﴿يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ﴾ [al-A'raf 54], meaning He covers it, and His words: ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى﴾ [al-Layl 1], meaning it covers and conceals; and examples of this are many.
So the meaning of His words ﴿إِذَا غَشِيَهُمْ﴾ is: it covered them, and it does not cover them except after rising above them. A wave (مَوْج) is what results from gathered water that rises until it covers the ships and drowns them.
As for His words ﴿كَالظُّلَلِ﴾, the author says: (the mountains that shade those beneath them). This is witnessed. God is greatest! When you see the sea with strong waves, you find the waters coming like mountains, and sometimes they clash and then a huge, very high crest rises from the sea. When such waves overspread them, ﴿دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾ [Luqman 32]: who are they? The disbelievers. They call upon God and ask Him, ﴿مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾, sincere to Him in religion. In this situation they do not ask anyone else. Would the worshipper of al-Lat say, "O Lat, save us"? No, because he knows what she cannot save him from. Nor the worshipper of al-'Uzza and Manat, nor the worshipper of Hubal, nor any of the other idols: it is impossible for him to call upon the idols in this state, because he knows they cannot save him; rather he calls upon God, Exalted, sincere to Him in religion.

As for His words ﴿لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾, what is meant by it is (that is: the supplication, that He may deliver them, meaning they do not call upon anyone along with Him). From where did the author take (they do not call upon anyone along with Him)? From His words ﴿مُخْلِصِينَ﴾, since sincerity (الإخلاص) means purification (التخليص), meaning that it is made for this thing alone. ﴿وَمَا أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ﴾ [al-Bayyinah 5]. In this state they know God and call upon Him. This shows that the shirk of those before was lighter than the shirk of those who came after. There are people now who, when a wave overspreads them like shades, or when harm befalls them, whom do they call upon? They call upon a created being. Instead of saying, "O God, save me," you find them saying, "O 'Ali, save me! O 'Abd al-Qadir, save me! O so-and-so, O so-and-so, save me!" So the shirk of these people has become uglier than the shirk of the first ones, because the first ones knew the truth when harm befell them, and that none removes that harm except God. As for these people, they increase in blindness upon their blindness. It is well known that neither 'Abd al-Qadir, nor al-Badawi, nor 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, nor others can remove the harm that befalls them; all of these, if harm afflicted them, could not remove it from themselves, so how could they remove it from others? This is in addition to the fact that they have died, and hope in them has been cut off in every respect. If they were alive and present, a person might seek their help and benefit from it; but if they are dead, can anyone seek their help except an ignorant person? It is not possible. Can 'Ali ibn Abi Talib come from his grave to save you, or 'Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani from his grave to save you, or al-Badawi from his grave to save you, or anyone else who is called upon in times of distress to save? Never. And God knows best. (...)

﴿مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾ means they do not call upon other than Him. ﴿فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ﴾ [Luqman 32]: "He delivered them to the land." This (...) is in the sense of conveying: He delivered them and brought them to the land. He did not say, "He delivered them from these shades only," but He delivered them with a deliverance by which they reached the shore of safety, to the land. The land here is the opposite of the sea, so it includes if He delivered them to a town, for the town in this verse is part of the land.

﴿فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ﴾: where is the answer to (لما), since (لما) here is conditional? The answer is ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مُقْتَصِدٌ﴾ [Luqman 32], meaning: and among them is one who is not moderate. So the answer is omitted, indicated by His words ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مُقْتَصِدٌ﴾; that is: when He delivered them to the land they divided into two groups: among them the moderate, and among them the disbeliever. (لما) has several meanings: it comes as conditional, it comes as a jussive negating particle, it comes in the sense of (إلا), and it comes in the sense of (حين) as a time adverb. These are four meanings.
It comes as conditional, as in this verse, and like His words: ﴿فَلَمَّا عَتَوْا عَنْ مَا نُهُوا عَنْهُ قُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ﴾ [al-A'raf 166]. It comes in the sense of (إلا) as in His words: ﴿إِنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمَّا عَلَيْهَا حَافِظٌ﴾ [al-Tariq 4], meaning: except that over it there is a guardian. It comes as a jussive negating particle, like His words: ﴿بَلْ لَمَّا يَذُوقُوا عَذَابِ﴾ [Sad 8], meaning: rather they have not yet tasted My punishment. And it comes as an adverb of time in the sense of (حين): you say, "I visited you when (لما) I heard of your arrival," meaning: when I heard of your arrival.

﴿فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ﴾ they divided into two groups; this answer is omitted. ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مُقْتَصِدٌ﴾: this (مِن) is partitive, meaning: some of them are moderate. He said: (midway between disbelief and belief), and among them is one who remains upon his disbelief. This is the second division. ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مُقْتَصِدٌ﴾ means: moderate. Moderation in everything is being midway in it. The meaning is that among them is one who becomes neither a believer nor a disbeliever: when he remembers God's blessing upon him in deliverance, he believes and thanks his Lord; but if safety deceives him, he disbelieves and transgresses, so he is moderate. And among them is the opposite. What is it? A disbeliever. Among them is a disbeliever.

The evidence that the opposite here means the disbeliever is His words: ﴿وَمَا يَجْحَدُ بِآيَاتِنَا إِلَّا كُلُّ خَتَّارٍ كَفُورٍ﴾ [Luqman 32]. Otherwise someone might say: who indicates to you that the opposite is the disbeliever? Could the opposite not be the believer, as in His words: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مُقْتَصِدٌ وَمِنْهُمْ سَابِقٌ بِالْخَيْرَاتِ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ [Fatir 32]? We say: this is possible, but His words ﴿وَمَا يَجْحَدُ بِآيَاتِنَا إِلَّا كُلُّ خَتَّارٍ كَفُورٍ﴾ show that the opposite of the moderate is whom? The disbeliever.

He said: ﴿وَمَا يَجْحَدُ بِآيَاتِنَا﴾. The word (الجحد) means denial and concealment, and it may be given the meaning of denial (التكذيب), as here, since it has been given the meaning of denial. The jahd that means concealment is transitive by itself, so one says "jahadahu," meaning he concealed it; but here it has been given the sense of denial, which is why it takes the preposition (ب), so it says ﴿وَمَا يَجْحَدُ بِآيَاتِنَا﴾, meaning: he does not deny them.

(Among them is deliverance from the wave, ﴿إِلَّا كُلُّ خَتَّارٍ﴾ treacherous, ﴿كَفُورٍ﴾ ungrateful for the blessings of God.) I seek refuge in God. None denies the signs of God, Mighty and Majestic, nor rejects them, nor calls them lies, except one who combines these two qualities: (الخَتْر), which is treachery, and the second, (الكُفْر), which is arrogance.

If someone asks: how is there treachery here? We say: because every human being has covenanted with his Lord: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى﴾ [al-A'raf 172], and God says: ﴿وَأَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِي أُوفِ بِعَهْدِكُمْ﴾ [al-Baqarah 40]. Every human being has covenanted with his Lord, by the requirement of his nature, to believe in Him. So when he disbelieves he becomes a treacherous one, does he not? He becomes treacherous; he did not fulfil the covenant.
﴿إِلَّا كُلُّ خَتَّارٍ كَفُورٍ﴾ for the blessings of God.

Then God, exalted, said: (﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ [Luqman 33], that is: the people of Makkah) (...).
He is the Lord, so He is the Creator, and since He is the Creator, He must be the one who is to be feared. It is as if He gives the reason for the command to piety: "Fear your Lord, because He is your Lord who brought you into being, prepared you, and sustained you." Here there is bringing into being, preparation, and provision. God brought mankind into being, and prepared them, that is, readied them for what they ought to be; and third, He supplied them with intellects and supplied them with messengers who brought the law of God.

(﴿اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ وَاخْشَوْا يَوْمًا لَا يَجْزِي﴾ does not avail ﴿وَالِدٌ عَنْ وَلَدِهِ﴾ [Luqman 33] anything.)
﴿وَاخْشَوْا يَوْمًا﴾: fear (الخشية) has been explained to us earlier as more specific than fear (الخوف), because it occurs together with knowledge of the one feared, by His words: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ﴾ [Fatir 28], and because it arises from the greatness of the one feared, whereas fear's cause is usually the weakness of the one who fears. So khashyah is lighter; meaning: fear this great day whose description is such and such, which God, Mighty and Majestic, has explained.

(﴿يَوْمًا لَا يَجْزِي وَالِدٌ عَنْ وَلَدِهِ﴾ anything.) The meaning of (يجزي) is (يُغْنِي), to avail. No one can ever ward off the evil of that day from his children. Although in this world, does he avail them and defend them? He does, and perhaps he throws himself into destruction for the sake of his children's lives; but in the Hereafter there is none of that. Rather a person flees from his brother, his mother and father, his spouse and his sons, fleeing from them for fear that they will cling to him because of a shortcoming in a right he neglected toward them: ﴿فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ فَلَا أَنْسَابَ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَلَا يَتَسَاءَلُونَ﴾ [al-Mu'minun 101]. No one asks about anyone; each says, "myself, myself," because the matter is so great. The mountains will be crumbled until they become scattered sand dunes, then they will become like carded wool, then they will be scattered and become dust blown about, dust flying in the air. So the matter is greater than that a parent could avail his child anything.

The word ﴿وَالِدٌ﴾ is indefinite in a negative context, and includes the father, the grandfather, the mother, and the grandmother, however far up they go.
﴿عَنْ وَلَدِهِ﴾: meaning the male? Which of them?
* A student: The male and the female.
* The Shaykh: The male and the female, because "walad" in the Arabic language applies to both male and female: ﴿يُوصِيكُمُ اللَّهُ فِي أَوْلَادِكُمْ لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ﴾ [al-Nisa' 11].

﴿لَا يَجْزِي وَالِدٌ عَنْ وَلَدِهِ وَلَا مَوْلُودٌ هُوَ جَازٍ عَنْ وَالِدِهِ شَيْئًا﴾ [Luqman 33]. He said: (﴿وَلَا مَوْلُودٌ هُوَ جَازٍ عَنْ وَالِدِهِ﴾ in it ﴿شَيْئًا﴾). His words ﴿مَوْلُودٌ﴾ may be the subject (مبتدأ), and ﴿هُوَ جَازٍ﴾ is this clause as the predicate of the subject; that is, ﴿مَوْلُودٌ﴾ is the first subject, ﴿هُوَ﴾ is a second subject, ﴿جَازٍ﴾ is the predicate of the second subject, and the clause made of the second subject and its predicate is in the place of a nominative predicate of the first subject. What made beginning with the indefinite noun in His words ﴿وَلَا مَوْلُودٌ﴾ permissible is that it occurs in a context of division. It may also be that His words ﴿وَلَا مَوْلُودٌ﴾ are conjoined to His words ﴿وَالِدٌ﴾, meaning: and no child avails anything; but on this reckoning the meaning of His words ﴿هُوَ جَازٍ عَنْ وَالِدِهِ شَيْئًا﴾ becomes problematic, since it becomes: "and no child who is one who avails for his father anything," so someone might think the expression is weak, but the matter is not so. The meaning of "and no child who is one who avails" is: no child who is, in capacity, fit to avail for his father; so ﴿هُوَ جَازٍ﴾ explains his quality, that he is qualified to avail his father something, yet he does not avail. On this reading the structure of the verse is not inconsistent, because what is negated in the first clause is the action, ﴿لَا يَجْزِي وَالِدٌ﴾, and in the second clause, what is its aspect?
* A student: "And no child avails."
* The Shaykh: "And no child"; because the implied wording is: "and no child avails." But His words ﴿هُوَ جَازٍ عَنْ وَالِدِهِ شَيْئًا﴾ contain an explanation that this child is qualified to avail.

If someone asks: why did he not restrict the father by this condition too? We say: because the father is usually qualified to avail, since the father is the elder, and it is possible for him to avail; unlike the child, who may be young and not understand anything, so for the child it was restricted by being qualified to avail.

So in His words ﴿وَلَا مَوْلُودٌ﴾ there are two readings grammatically; one of them is?
* A student: "﴿مَوْلُودٌ﴾, this has two readings."
* The Shaykh: Its parsing has two aspects.
* The student: Yes, the first aspect: that (مولود) is the subject, (هو) is a second subject, and (جاز) is the predicate of the second subject.
* The Shaykh: And the clause?
* The student: And the clause of the second subject and its predicate is in the place of the predicate of the first subject.
* The Shaykh: In the place of nominative...
* Student: Nominative predicate of the first subject.
* The Shaykh: The first; this is one aspect.
* Student: And the second aspect is that the last clause is conjoined to...
* The Shaykh: No, that ﴿مَوْلُودٌ﴾ is conjoined to what?

**Student:** On ﴿wālidun﴾ [the reading with the nominative].

**Shaykh:** On ﴿wālidun﴾. The clause ﴿huwa jāzin⁠﻿ ʿan wālidihi shayʾan﴾ is a description of ﴿mawlūdun﴾. On the first view there is no problem in the meaning, but there is a problem in the change of the *naẓm*, meaning the change of style: for the father he used a verb, and for the child he used a nominal sentence. The answer to this is that he used a nominal sentence for the child so that none of the Muslims, who had embraced Islam, would hope that their children could suffice for them in anything. That is, so that a Muslim child would not hope to be relieved from his disbelieving father, He used a nominal sentence, which indicates permanence and continuity.

The second view: we said it is coordinated with ﴿wālidun⁠﻿﴾. On this view a problem arises in His saying ﴿huwa jāzin ʿan wālidihi shayʾan﴾, since the meaning would become: "nor will a child who is able to repay on behalf of his father repay anything." We said: the answer to this is that the meaning of ﴿huwa jāzin⁠﻿﴾ is: he is capable of repaying, for he has the means, but on that Day he will not repay, even though he is among those able to repay, or among those deserving of recompense.

﴿Nor a child who can repay on behalf of his father anything.⁠﻿﴾ So what benefits a person on that Day? What benefits him is what Allah mentioned about Abraham, the Friend (*Khalīl*), upon him be peace: ﴿And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected, the Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart⁠﻿﴾ [ash-Shuʿarāʾ 26:87–89]. This is the one who benefits: the one who comes to Allah with a sound heart, that is, sound from everything that diminishes it, from shirk and what is less than it.

He says: (﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah is true⁠﻿﴾ [Luqmān 31:33] concerning the resurrection). That is, concerning the resurrection and what is in it, not the resurrection alone, but the resurrection, the reckoning and the recompense, good and evil. ﴿True⁠﻿﴾ means established and certain. This is among what is included in His saying, ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth⁠﻿﴾ [Luqmān 31:30]: from His being the Truth is that His promise, glory be to Him, is true. The promise of others may be true or may be false and unfulfilled, because others than Allah, may break their promise either due to lying in the one who promises, or due to inability. A man says to you: "I will bring you, right after the afternoon prayer, a plate of bread," or "a plate of bread is not suitable."

**Student:** If it is with broth, it is suitable.

**Shaykh:** It is suitable?

**Student:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** With broth.

**Student:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** A plate of bread and a cup of broth. After the afternoon prayer he does not bring you anything, though he has plates of bread and cups of broth. But he did not bring it to you. Why? Because he lied. The next day he did not bring you anything, because he had nothing: he has no money to buy with, and nothing in the house. This one also broke his appointment, why? Due to inability. And forgetting is also a form of inability, because forgetfulness is, in reality, a deficiency in a person.

So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, His promise is true and must come to pass: ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah is true.⁠﻿﴾ The author said: (concerning the resurrection). The correct understanding is: concerning the resurrection and other things that will occur on that Day, of reckoning and recompense.

(﴿So let not the worldly life deceive you⁠﻿﴾ from Islam, ﴿and let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah⁠﻿﴾ in His forbearance and His respite: the Shayṭān.)

﴿So let not the worldly life deceive you⁠﻿﴾: here the verb is emphasized with the energetic *nūn* (*nūn at-tawkīd*). What type of emphasis is this in this verb: obligatory?

**Student:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** Obligatory. Do you agree with your brother?

**Student:** No, it is not obligatory.

**Shaykh:** It is not obligatory? When is it obligatory?

**Student:** It is obligatory under four conditions: an affirmative (...).

**Shaykh:** And this.

**Student:** This is negated.

**Shaykh:** It is not so. No, this is a prohibition, but it does not occur in the answer to an oath. That is, as long as it is in the answer to an oath it is obligatory, so this is among the non-obligatory cases, but it is frequent.

He says: ﴿So let not the worldly life deceive you⁠﻿﴾. *Ghurūr* is deception. That is: do not let it deceive you with its adornments, its pleasures and its joys. What does it mean?

**Student:** From Islam.

**Shaykh:** From Islam and its laws: from Islam if the person is a disbeliever, and from its laws if he is a Muslim.

In His saying, ﴿So let not the worldly life deceive you⁠﻿﴾, there is discouragement of this life, because He said *ad-dunyā*. *Ad-dunyā* is the feminine form (*fuʿlā*) from *ad-dunuww* (nearness), and it is near in time and near in meaning and rank. It is called *dunyā* because it precedes the Hereafter, and *dunyā* because it is deficient, as you say: "this is less than this," meaning it is lower than it.

His saying, ﴿So let not the worldly life deceive you⁠﻿﴾, with emphasis, is evidence that its deception is severe. Therefore the prohibition was emphasized with the *nūn*: ﴿So let not [it] deceive you⁠﻿﴾.

﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah⁠﻿﴾. The author said: (﴿concerning Allah⁠﻿﴾ means: His forbearance and His respite). That is: "let them not deceive you concerning Allah": the matter is as the author said, meaning through His respite and His forbearance. *Al-ghaṛūr* is an adjectival form (*ṣifa mushabbaha*), and what is meant by it is: what? The Shayṭān, as Allah said: ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires, but Satan promises them only deception⁠﻿﴾ [an-Nisāʾ 4:120]. The Shayṭān deceives a person concerning Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He says to him: "If you were upon falsehood, Allah would punish you." This is one. Or he says to him: "Indeed, the mercy of Allah is vast, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." Or he gives him false hopes of repentance, saying: "True, this is a sin, and the person exposes himself to punishment, but repentance is ahead of you. Now enjoy this sin, and afterward repent." Among this is what some people give him false hope of, saying: "Do not pray until you reach forty years of age." This exists among some people. Some foreigners say that their families tell them: "Prayer is not obligatory upon you until you reach forty years." For this reason they always ask about past prayers: do they make them up or not? This is from the deception of the Shayṭān. Also from the deception of the Shayṭān is that he says to him, about a thing he believes to be a sin: "This is a matter of disagreement. As long as there is disagreement, go ahead and do it," even though he believes it is a sin.

Likewise, from his deception is that he says, about an obligatory matter which the person believes to be obligatory: "This is a matter of disagreement." Then this man, if he needs the forbidden, says: "It is a matter of disagreement," and does it. And if he does not need it, he says: "What I hold as my religion is that this is forbidden, and I will not do it." So this thing becomes a religion yesterday and not a religion today. Or he says, for example, if the obligatory matter agrees with his desire: "By Allah, this is obligatory, I must do it." It is not permissible. The Muslim is bound by the rulings of Allah. But when something comes up for him that day, he says: "It is a matter of disagreement, and I am at ease, since it is disputed and not definitively settled."

An example of this: praying in the mosque in congregation. Is this a matter of disagreement or not? The congregational prayer itself is disputed, and whether it is in the mosque is also disputed. He believes that praying in the mosque in congregation is obligatory, and that a person may not leave the congregation, nor may he pray it in congregation in his house. But if something comes up for him, what does he choose? "It is a matter of disagreement. We want to pray this way. Come on, everyone, let us pray." And if something comes up for him, or if no one is with him, he says: "The congregational prayer is a matter of disagreement. Since it is disputed, I want to pray by myself and (...) the work."

The summary: this is from the deception of the Shayṭān. Also from the deception of the Shayṭān is that he gives a ruling to people one way and gives himself a ruling another way: he grants himself concessions and makes things easy for himself, but is strict with others. All such matters are from the deception of the Shayṭān. What is obligatory is that a person be upon one religion: the religion of Allah, for himself and for others, and in all his conditions.

**Student:** The opposite of the last point.

**Shaykh:** What is it?

**Student:** If he makes things easy for people and is strict with himself.

**Shaykh:** If he is strict with himself as a means of disciplining himself, there is no harm, as long as he believes that the ruling of Allah is ease. But he is strict with himself out of scrupulousness (*tawarruʿ*), and it has a basis in the evidence, so there is no harm.

**Student:** If the matter is disputed and he sees that the easier is that it... he means...

**Shaykh:** For example, some people are scrupulous about certain foods: they do not eat them themselves, but they do not tell people, "Do not eat them," because they have no evidence. Or they are scrupulous about certain perfumes: they refrain from them, but they do not forbid them to people, because there is no evidence for it. Or, for example, he binds himself to doing something, though the texts do not clearly make it obligatory. So he does not make it obligatory for people, but he does not like to neglect it. There is no harm in this, because there is no desire in it. The problem is desire: that he makes things easy for himself and is strict with people.

But what is your opinion if he says: "I permit this act for myself, because I control myself. I do not exceed what is lawful. And I forbid it to people, because if I allowed it for them they would exceed what is lawful. So I prohibit it to prevent them from exceeding what is lawful, while for myself I have vowed not to go beyond what is lawful."

**Student:** Then there is no harm.

**Shaykh:** We say: do not say, "It is forbidden for people," but say: "I fear for you that you may exceed, and the like." But if you say, "It is forbidden," and you go and forbid this man from this thing while you enjoy it as you please, this is not acceptable. Rather say to him: "I fear for you that you may exceed what is lawful, or that people who imitate you may exceed by it," and the like, until the matter becomes clear to him that the ruling of Allah concerning it is lawful, but that it is feared people will go beyond it. And Allah knows best. (...)

He expressed it with *mā* rather than *man*, because *man* specifies the person: a rational being. If it is not rational, one says *mā*. As for what relates to attributes and actions, these are expressed with *mā*. I gave you an example of this in His saying: ﴿So marry what seems good to you of women⁠﻿﴾ [an-Nisāʾ 4:3], rather than *man ṭāba*.

﴿And He knows what is in the wombs⁠﻿﴾. *Al-arḥām* is the plural of *raḥim* (womb), which is the container of the fetus. The fetus is enclosed by three walls: the abdomen, the womb and the placenta. The placenta is this vessel around the fetus. And this vessel, glory be to the Mighty God, is a strange substance: it is neither purely watery nor purely solid, but slippery and smooth, so that the movement of the fetus is easy. Now, cars that have *yāyāt*, and I think you know what *yāyāt* are, are soft and move with great ease. This, by Allah's permission, is the strange substance inside the fetal vessel.

**Student:** The vessel (...) the *yāyāt*.

**Shaykh:** *Yāyāt*? *Yāyāt* is a colored strip.

**Student:** (...).

**Shaykh:** By Allah, I do not know.

**Student:** (...).

**Shaykh:** In any case, I say: this substance, glory be to the Mighty God, is for facilitating the movement of the fetus, so that its mother does not feel fatigue, and it also does not feel fatigue. And this, in any case, Allah is Knowing and Wise, may He be exalted.

These are the three darknesses, as Allah said: ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in three darknesses⁠﻿﴾ [az-Zumar 39:6]. And He said: ﴿So We placed him in a firm resting place⁠﻿﴾ [al-Mursalāt 77:21], meaning that nothing that harms this fetus can enter, neither air nor anything else.

﴿He knows what is in the wombs⁠﻿﴾. We have said: the object of this knowledge (*mutaʿallaq*) is whether it is male or female, and likewise what relates to attributes: whether it will be happy or wretched, whether it will be doing righteous or wicked deeds, whether its provision will be abundant or restricted, whether its life will be long or short. All of these relate to the knowledge of embryos. Some of it can never be known, and no one knows it except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And some of it can be known, like matters that are observed and perceived. This can be known, and they have now reached it by what they have reached.

But can they know whether this fetus is male or female before it is formed? Until now they have not reached that. We do not say "no." We say: until now they have not reached it. I have heard that some of them argue for whether it is male or female from the sperm itself: that the male has a particular characteristic and the female has a particular characteristic. If this is correct, do not ask "from where?"

**Student:** The ovum must be fertilized (...).

**Shaykh:** I have now heard this, and they have also photographed it. They photographed this: they say that the male sperm has a particular radiation, which travels in a particular radiation, and this one has a particular radiation. And Allah knows best. In any case, if they reach that, we say: no one knows whether it will be determined as male or female except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Then the other conditions we mentioned, which relate to the knowledge of embryos, they cannot know.

**Student:** But Shaykh, is this guesswork or...

**Shaykh:** No, it is observation. They now have powerful rays that are directed at everything.

I mentioned to you in our discussion of this verse in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, and I said: we must not contradict a thing in this way, rejecting it outright. We must be patient, because if we reject this thing and say, "This is impossible," and then it turns out to be established according to modern sciences, what does that lead to? It leads to rejecting the Qur'an, or to doubting it. And we know that two certain matters cannot contradict each other at all. This is impossible.

**Student:** Alright, for example, the verse in Sūrat an-Najm: ﴿And that He created the two mates, the male and the female, from a sperm-drop when it is emitted⁠﻿﴾. The word *idhā* means "at a time," ﴿when it is emitted⁠﻿﴾ means "in the state of..."

**Shaykh:** By Allah, in any case this is possible: ﴿And that He created the two mates, the male and the female, from a sperm-drop when it is emitted⁠﻿﴾ [an-Najm 53:45–46] can be said to mean that He created it from a sperm-drop in the state of its being emitted, that is, poured forth, and that this will be the male or the female, but it will only become clear afterward.

**Student:** The sperm-drop is for the female?

**Shaykh:** Yes, the female is created from the sperm-drop.

**Student:** I mean: or rather, like a person who tries these things, does he care about knowing...

**Shaykh:** About knowing?

**Student:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** Knowing what?

**Student:** Since He said, ﴿He knows what is in the wombs⁠﻿﴾, we tried to know what is in the wombs.

**Shaykh:** ﴿He knows what is in the wombs⁠﻿﴾, but did He say, "Do not know it"? We now know it, since we have reached knowledge of it by these means (...).

Also, we have a problem with ﴿And He sends down the rain⁠﻿﴾, which we raised in the lesson but have now forgotten, and now I have remembered it. These predictions they make, that there will be rain tomorrow: is this from the knowledge of the unseen or not?

**Student:** No.

**Shaykh:** We mentioned that it is not from the knowledge of the unseen, but is a forecast by means of precise instruments by which they know the state of the atmosphere and whether it is suitable to be rainy or not. For this reason, sometimes the matter is not as they predicted, is it? Moreover, they cannot predict rain years in advance; at most it is for a short period.

**Student:** Shaykh, the test-tube baby. I think you have heard of the test-tube baby?

**Shaykh:** There is nothing in this. If the woman is his wife, there is no harm in it. But if it is the sperm of a foreign man, this is forbidden and not permissible.

**Student:** Is there not a hadith, in terms of the knowledge of the male, that if the man's sperm rises over the woman's, they say it reaches... that this (...) if it rises...

**Shaykh:** The man's water is (...) the woman's water.

**Student:** Those who know this (...) they argue from it.

**Shaykh:** The point is, in any case, if we reach knowledge of this, it does not contradict the noble verse, because there are matters concerning the fetus that no one can reach knowledge of.

He said: ﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow⁠﻿﴾. The word *nafs* here is indefinite in a negative context, and *tadrī* means "knows." The *nafs* here is indefinite in a negative context, generalizing every soul: any soul does not know what it will earn tomorrow. Even if he is among the cleverest people at managing and organizing his time, he does not know what he will earn tomorrow. Or does he? And he knows what others will earn?

**Students:** This is the unseen.

**Shaykh:** A fortiori. If a soul does not know what it will earn, then it does not know what others will earn, a fortiori. Therefore, it does not know what Allah will do, yes, a fortiori: if it cannot know what pertains to the knowledge of the created, how can it know what pertains to the knowledge of the Creator? So it is a fortiori that it does not know it.

Therefore no one knows what they will gain tomorrow, whether good or evil, wealth or children, or anything else. A person may expect something, but it does not come to him. It is turned away from him, or something comes between him and it, so he does not reach what he has earned.

His saying ﴿what he will earn tomorrow﴾: what is meant by "tomorrow"? Is it the day immediately following your day, or the whole future? What is meant is the whole future. You do not know what you will earn in it, even if it is far off. This is based on the saying of God Most High: ﴿O you who have believed, fear God, and let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow﴾ [al-Hashr 18]. Does it mean Sunday after Saturday? No, it means the Day of Resurrection. Every future time may rightly be called "tomorrow."

﴿What he will earn tomorrow﴾: the word ﴿tomorrow﴾ is in the accusative case, and it is the object of ﴿earn﴾. Is it an object of the direct kind, or of the indirect kind, or an adverbial object of time, place, or accompaniment?
* Students: It is an adverbial object of time.
* Another student: Sheikh, it is an absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq).
* The Sheikh: What do you say? These are two opinions: one says it is an absolute object, and the other says it is an adverbial object of time? It is an adverbial object of time (maf'ul fihi), because it is a time expression. That is: "what he will earn in tomorrow." Have you not heard the words of the poet:
"I know the knowledge of today and of yesterday before it,
but about the knowledge of what is in tomorrow, I am blind."

So it is an adverbial expression of time. ﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die﴾ [Luqman 34]. The word ﴿soul﴾ is, as we said regarding the first ﴿soul﴾, an indefinite noun in a negative context, so it covers every soul. No soul knows in what land it will die: will it be in the land where it was born, or near it, or far from it? It does not know. Nor does it know in what time it will die, and this is even more so. Place offers a person some choice. Does he not? He chooses to be here, or he chooses to be there, or he chooses to be in a third place. But time is not something over which you have any choice. If you do not know the place where you will die, even though you have some choice regarding it, then it is even more fitting that you do not know the time when you will die. This is part of the wisdom of God, Mighty and Majestic, that He has concealed from the human being the day on which he will die, or the place where God knows he will die. If a person knew this, he would be anxious throughout his life. His only concern would be: "Today has gone, and only so many years remain, or so many months, or so many days," and he would suffer tremendously. But now, every day that comes upon a person, he says: (...). Perhaps his end is closer than the strap of his sandal. But what matters is that he has hope for a long life, and he does not pay attention to this matter at all. He does not pay attention to it because he knows that he has no knowledge of it, and that its knowledge is with God, Mighty and Majestic. This is from the mercy of God, Mighty and Majestic, toward us.

Does a person estimate that he will die in such-and-such a land, or does he not estimate it? He may estimate it. Sometimes, when someone is told, "Will you not travel?" he says, "Never. My town is where I live and where I die." But when his end draws near, he travels. Some need arises for him until he is carried to the land where he is to die. I know a man who never left his town of 'Unayzah, for many years. When he fell ill, it was decided that his treatment would be in Egypt. He had never left 'Unayzah, except I think once for the Hajj, and he had no intention of it. He grew old and his life came to an end. But, glory be to God, when God willed to bring him to the land where he was to die, he was taken to Egypt and died there. I know many people who were taken to distant places they never imagined they would go. I have also mentioned to you the story told to me by a trustworthy person: a sick woman whom they brought back from the Hajj. When they were in the Ri' (the wilderness of the mountains surrounding the Hijaz), they stopped one night, and in the morning they loaded their camels, thinking they were going to move on. This man had his mother with him, and she was sick. He wanted to... he remained behind to prepare the place for her on the mount. The people went on while he was in his place. When he had finished what he wanted to finish in preparing a place for his mother and she mounted, she set off. But they lost him; he did not know where they had gone. He entered the Ri' with her, walking and walking, hearing no sound and with no one around him, until he reached a tent, a small Bedouin dwelling. He stopped with them and asked them about the way. They said, "The way is behind you." He said, "I'll wait a little." When he got down, glory be to God the Mighty, and lowered his mother, she died in that very place, which neither he nor anyone else had estimated he would reach. But in order for this woman to be carried to the land of her death, the causes came together as they did.

Likewise, you see accidents today. A person in his town does not estimate that he will die in some place in the desert, yet he is taken to the place where he will die, to the point that he dies in that exact place, on the very grains of dust that were decreed for him. This is a matter that is observed.

Likewise, regarding time, a person does not know when he will die. It may be delayed by mere moments, in order that his term and his period be completed. There are evidences for this, and among them is what I have related to you. Perhaps some of you were not present. Here in 'Unayzah, it happened that a man came in his car on the main road, and there were two young men on animals who had come from another crossing road. When each of them approached the point of meeting, they stopped to wait for the other to cross. Each of them said, "The other is not going to cross; I want to go." Everyone moved on, and the car struck the rear of the two young men with the animal, and he died instantly. Why did he stop this stop, which lasted only moments? In order that the appointed time be completed. (...)

(﴿And He sends down﴾ with the light and the intensive forms.) ("He sends down" [yunzil] and "He causes to descend" [yunazzil]), and both have come in the Qur'an. ﴿He sends down water from the sky﴾ [al-An'am 99] is on the light reading. He said: God Most High has said: ﴿And He sends down for you provision from the sky﴾ [Ghafir 13]. ﴿Sends down﴾ here is on the intensive reading.

He says: (﴿the rain﴾ at a time He knows). The evidence is in the author's words "at a time He knows." That is the evidence. That is, the author clarified that the meaning of sending down the rain is at the time He knows, so that this is part of the knowledge of the unseen.

(﴿And He knows what is in the wombs﴾: whether male or female, and none knows any of the three except God, Most High.) The restriction to "male or female" in ﴿He knows what is in the wombs﴾ is open to question, because knowledge of what is in the wombs is not limited to the male and female only. It is more general than that. This has been mentioned earlier in the tafsir (...).

The wisdom in using "what" (ma) rather than "who" (man)... (...). And his saying: (none knows any of the three except God) is true before its formation is possible. But after it forms, others besides God know it. This angel knows whether it is male or female.

(﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow﴾: good or evil.) But what God knows is what is known. For this reason he said: (and God Most High knows it).

(﴿And no soul knows in what land it will die﴾; and God knows it, ﴿surely God is All-Knowing﴾ of everything, ﴿All-Aware﴾ of its inner reality as of its outer appearance.)

Which is more specific, "All-Aware" (Khabir) or "All-Knowing" ('Alim)? "All-Aware" is more specific, because knowledge relates to the outer and the inner, while awareness relates to the inner. For this reason he said: (All-Aware of its inner reality as of its outer appearance), because one who knows the inner reality is more fitting to know the outer appearance.

Then he said: (Al-Bukhari narrated[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (4627).]] from Ibn 'Umar, the hadith: "The keys to the unseen are five," ﴿Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour﴾ [Luqman 34], to the end of the surah).

﴿And He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die﴾. We explained in the commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari the reason these are called keys. We said: The Hour is a key to... and so on. The sending down of rain is a key to life, the life of the earth and the plants. Knowing what is in the wombs is a key to...?
* A student: (...).
* The Sheikh: No, something else.
* The student: (...).
* The Sheikh: Yes, it is a key to the life of the human being and the beginning of his creation. The first thing he passes through after formation is the womb. For this reason, the human being has four abodes: the first is in his mother's belly, the second is in this world, the third is in the barzakh (the intermediate state), and the fourth is in the Hereafter. ﴿That is the Abode of the Hereafter. We assign it to those who do not desire haughtiness on earth or corruption, and the good outcome is for the righteous﴾ [al-Qasas 83].

﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow﴾ is a key to work in the future. ﴿And no soul knows in what land it will die﴾ is a key to the Hereafter with regard to the death of each particular person. (...)

﴿And that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and that God is the Most High, the Great﴾ [Luqman 30].
* From this verse is derived, first, that God is the Truth, and truth is the opposite of falsehood. Falsehood is everything that has no benefit and no good in it.
* And from it is derived that everything that issues from God is true. From where is this taken? Because only truth issues from the Truth.
* And from the noble verse is derived that worship of other than God is false (...).

And greatness: ﴿and that God is the Most High, the Great﴾.

Then God Most High said: ﴿Do you not see that the ships sail through the sea by the favor of God﴾ to the end [Luqman 31]. In this verse, the addressee is reminded of this blessing, which is the sailing of ships on the sea by the favor of God.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the sailing of ships on this flowing water, though they carry heavy loads, is a blessing from God, based on the reading that the "bi" (by) indicates causation.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: God Most High's care for creation in conveying His signs to them, from His saying: ﴿so that He may show you some of His signs﴾.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: signs benefit only those who combine patience and gratitude, from His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for every patient, grateful one﴾: patient in adversity, and grateful in ease.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: God's signs are divided into sensory and non-sensory. Is the ship sailing in the sea sensory or non-sensory? Sensory. God has made it one of His signs: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs﴾.

Then the Mighty and Majestic said, clarifying the condition of these deniers: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ to the end [Luqman 32]. In this there is evidence (...) 
* Among the benefits of the verse: sending waves from God, Mighty and Majestic, is a trial for the servants, from His saying: ﴿when it covers them﴾, ﴿they call upon God﴾. He tests them: do they only know God in hardship, or in both hardship and ease?
* Among the benefits of the verse: establishing the prophethood of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, from His saying: ﴿when a wave covers them like shadows﴾. The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, had not boarded the sea so as to know these waves and that they are like shadows. But he, peace and blessings be upon him, knew of them from the report of God. ﴿When a wave covers them like shadows﴾. For this reason some scholars said: the fact that this verse conveys the description of the sea and the waves covering it, as though the Messenger ﷺ were describing it, indicates that he is truly the Messenger of God, because he had never boarded the sea. And one should not say that he may have been informed of it, because God refuted this with His saying: ﴿And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, but this is clear Arabic speech﴾ [al-Nahl 103].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: when these polytheists fell into hardship, they knew God.
* From this follows that knowledge of God in such a state does not suffice. For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Get to know God in ease, and He will know you in hardship."[[Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (6437) with this wording, and narrated by Ahmad (2803) with the wording: "Get to know Him in ease, He will know you in hardship," from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both.]]
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the polytheists acknowledge Lordship, from His saying: ﴿they call upon God﴾. They do not call upon Him except while knowing that He is able to rescue them. Otherwise, one could not call upon one whom he does not believe to be able.
* Among its benefits: the polytheists of the past were in a better state than the polytheists today. Because the polytheists today, when hardship befalls them, whom do they call upon? They call upon their gods besides God. They call upon such-and-such a saint, such-and-such a companion, and the like. But the polytheists of the past called upon God alone.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: God, Mighty and Majestic, answers their supplication, although He knows they will disbelieve. Or is that not so?
* Students: Yes.
* The Sheikh: From His saying: ﴿But none denies Our signs except every treacherous ingrate﴾, and He, glory be to Him, knows that.
* Among its benefits: the answering of the supplication of one in distress, even if he is a disbeliever. Or is that not so?
* Students: Yes.
* The Sheikh: Because God answered their supplication even though He knew they were disbelievers and would disbelieve. This is supported by the general meaning of His saying: ﴿Who answers the distressed one when he calls upon Him?﴾ [al-Naml 62]. He did not say "the believer," but said "the distressed one," which is general. Likewise, the supplication of the wronged one is answered even if he is a disbeliever, based on the general meaning of the Messenger's, peace and blessings be upon him, saying to Mu'adh ibn Jabal: "Beware the supplication of the wronged, for there is no barrier between it and God."[[Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (6437) with this wording, and narrated by Ahmad (2803) with the wording: "Get to know Him in ease, He will know you in hardship," from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both.]]
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: whoever is saved from some calamity, either he will fulfill what is incumbent upon him and so be moderate, or he will return to his disbelief and so be a treacherous deceiver. For when he called upon God, sincere to Him in religion, in a time of hardship, the consequence was that there should be a covenant between him and God that he would remain upon it. If he disbelieves, he becomes treacherous and betraying.
* A student: Sheikh, is it not derived from it that after the polytheist sees the punishment, if he would return, he would return (...)?
* The Sheikh: But this is mentioned in Surat al-An'am: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am 28].
* The student: As long as he called upon God and was sincere, then (...).
* The Sheikh: It indicates that the disbeliever is a disbeliever: in hardship he is sincere, and in ease he disbelieves, and we seek refuge in God.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the power of God, Mighty and Majestic, from His saying: ﴿But when He had delivered them﴾.
* Among its benefits: the establishment of His knowledge.
* Among its benefits: the establishment of His hearing. Hearing, knowledge, and power: from where are they derived? From His saying: ﴿But when He had delivered them﴾, because He does not deliver them when they call upon Him unless He has heard their supplication and knows their state, and is able to remove their harm.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: whoever keeps his covenant does not deny the signs of God, from His saying: ﴿And none denies Our signs except every treacherous ingrate﴾.
* Among its benefits: a warning against betrayal, for it may be a cause of what? Of disbelief and denial. For this reason the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The sign of the hypocrite is three," and he mentioned among them: "When he makes a covenant, he betrays."[[This is a hadith composed of two hadiths. His saying ﷺ "When he makes a covenant, he betrays" is part of the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, may God be pleased with them, raised to the Prophet: "Four qualities, whoever has them is a pure hypocrite..." The hadith is agreed upon: al-Bukhari (34) and Muslim (58/106). As for the hadith "The sign of the hypocrite is three," it does not mention betrayal. It is agreed upon: al-Bukhari (33) and Muslim (59), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him.]] So if none denies the signs except the treacherous, this means that betrayal is a cause of denial and disbelief.

Then God Most High said: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord and dread a Day when no father will avail his son at all﴾ to the end.
* From the noble verse is derived the obligation of fearing God. The evidence: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord﴾, a command. Especially since it is joined with warning about the Last Day in His saying: ﴿and dread a Day﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 31, verse 30–34 (part 5 of 5):

* Among its benefits: the affirmation of the Last Day, from His saying: ﴿And fear a Day⦆ — for had its reality not been established, one would not have been warned against it.
* Among them: that on this Day no close relative will avail his close relative. Or not?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Alright. If someone said: "Did Allah mention only the father and the child?"
We say: if the benefit of a father from his child, and of a child from his father, is negated, then others are negated all the more so; for the child is a part (baḍʿah) of his father, so if the part does not benefit from the whole, and the whole does not benefit from its part, then all the more so (...).
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the emphasis on this Day and its certain occurrence, from His saying: ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah is true⦆.
* Among its benefits: the warning against the world, its deceit and its delusion, from His saying: ﴿So let not the worldly life deceive you⦆.
* Among them: that the world is among the greatest causes that come between a person and his fear of the Last Day, because He made fear of the Day a consequence of it, saying: ﴿And fear a Day⦆, then said: ﴿So let not⦆; ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, so let not you be deceived⦆. And so it is.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the warning against Satan, from His saying: ﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you about Allah⦆.
* Among its benefits also: that Satan is a great deceiver, from His saying: ﴿the Deceiver⦆. It is either an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālaghah) or an attributive adjective (ṣifah mushabbahah), and both indicate permanence and abundance.
* Student: (...) Satan. Is there no deceiver other than Satan?
* The Shaykh: No, he [Ibn 'Abbas or the exegete] explained it that way, and it is possible that it includes even the devils of mankind, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy — devils from mankind and jinn, inspiring to one another decorative speech in delusion⦆ [al-An'am 112].
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: If he deceives you away from the truth, then he is one of the devils of mankind. But the apparent meaning of the verse, "the Deceiver," is that this is a necessary attribute, and it is possible that this refers to Satan.
Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, with Allah is knowledge of the Hour⦆ to the end.
* From this noble verse is derived, firstly: that knowledge of the Hour is among the exclusive attributes of Allah's knowledge alone, from His saying: ﴿with Him is knowledge of the Hour⦆, and this indicates restriction (ḥaṣr).
* And from it: the demonstration of Allah the Mighty and Majestic's favour in sending down rain, as in His saying: ﴿and He sends down the rain⦆. And the one who sends down a thing is the one who knows it, so it is derived from this that Allah the Exalted is exclusively the one who knows the descent of rain.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that knowledge of what is in the wombs belongs to Allah alone, from His saying: ﴿and He knows⦆ (...).
This is the correct view. When we consider the apparent context: ﴿and He knows what is in the wombs⦆ does not negate that others may know; because Allah's knowing (...), but the Messenger's explanation, peace and blessings be upon him, that these are the keys of the unseen which none knows except Allah, indicates that none knows what is in the wombs except Allah.
If someone asks: why was it not phrased as: "and none knows what is in the wombs except Allah," in this form?
The answer — and Allah knows best — is that since knowledge of the fetus may be attainable in some circumstances, He said: ﴿and He knows what is in the wombs⦆.
* Among the benefits of the verses: that a human being does not know the unseen of the future: ﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow⦆. So if a person does not know what he himself will earn, then his ignorance of what is decreed for him by Allah is all the more so, and his ignorance of what others will earn is all the more so. On this basis, if a claimant claimed that Allah the Exalted will decree such-and-such for this man, we are certain that he is a liar, because none knows what is in tomorrow except Allah. When one of the women said in the presence of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: "And among us is a prophet who knows what is in tomorrow," he forbade her and said: "Say what you were saying before" [[Al-Bukhari (4001) transmitted with his chain from al-Rubayyi' bint Mu'awwidh, who said: The Prophet ﷺ entered upon me on the morning of my wedding night and sat on my bed as you are sitting near me, and young girls were beating the tambourine and lamenting those of their fathers who were killed at Badr, until a girl said: "And among us is a prophet who knows what is in tomorrow." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do not say this; say what you were saying."]]. And it is not permissible for the Messenger or anyone else to be claimed to know what is in tomorrow.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a person does not know in what land he will die, from His saying: ﴿And no soul knows in what land it will die⦆.
* Among its benefits: that death occurs only on land, or is it possible otherwise? ﴿And no soul knows in what land it will die⦆.
* Student: It must be on land.
* The Shaykh: It must be on land?
* The Student: One may die, but the resting place (...).
* The Shaykh: The one in the car... We mentioned in the tafsir that the one in the car is on land. But can it be said that someone could die above gravity?
* Student: (...) in space.
* The Shaykh: In space? There is a possibility, but it is not apparent; because His saying: ﴿in what land it will die⦆ may be based on what is usual. Yet we have a verse in the Qur'an where Allah the Exalted says: ﴿In it you will live, and in it you will die, and from it you will be brought forth⦆ [al-A'raf 25]. The fronting of the complement, which is the adverbial phrase ﴿in it⦆, indicates restriction, and this is the default. If it later becomes clear that one of them dies in space and does not return to the earth, for example, then this would be based on the overwhelming majority. Until now we have not heard that anyone has died in space; we have not heard that anyone has died above gravity. Rather, even if he dies, the apparent meaning is that he must return.
* Student: The soul (...).
* The Shaykh: No, it is not restricted to the soul; the body itself: ﴿And no soul knows in what land it will die⦆.
Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted⦆.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that no one knows when he will die. From where is this taken? From the fact that our ignorance of the place of our death entails our ignorance of the time of our death; indeed, ignorance of the time is more fitting.
* Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, al-'Alim (the All-Knowing) and al-Khabir (the All-Aware), and the attributes of knowledge and awareness that they contain.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that whoever claims knowledge of anything that Allah has made exclusive to His knowledge is a disbeliever, because he contradicts Allah the Exalted, and contradicting Allah is disbelief.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 31, verse 30–34 (part 1 of 5):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth﴾ [Luqman 30]. "That" refers to what was mentioned earlier of the subjugation of the sun and the moon, and the power to resurrect and to create; that is, that aforementioned matter.

"Because Allah is the Truth": the "bi" (ba') here denotes causation (lil-sababiyyah); that is, because Allah is the Truth. By virtue of His being the Truth, these matters came into being and these systems were ordered, for He, may He be exalted, is Truth in His essence, Truth in His actions, Truth in His judgments, and Truth in His names and attributes. His Messenger is true, His Book is true, His promise is true, His reward is true, His punishment is true, and everything that proceeds from Him is true.

Al-haqq (the Truth) is the opposite of al-batil (falsehood), and al-batil is vain and idle talk or action that contains no good. So the meaning is that everything that proceeds from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is true and established good.

﴿And that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood﴾ [Luqman 30]. "And that" (wa-anna) is conjoined to "that" (anna); meaning: "and [that it is because]," conjoined to the opening "anna."

His saying "mā yad'ūn" (what they invoke): "mā" here is a relative pronoun; meaning: "and that which they invoke."

His saying "yad'ūn" (they invoke) includes both du'a' al-'ibadah (invocation of worship) and du'a' al-mas'alah (invocation of petition), because the idols that are worshipped besides Allah are called upon in the sense of being worshipped, and are called upon in the sense of being asked.

Du'a' (invocation) has two meanings: du'a' of worship and du'a' of petition. The saying of the Exalted: ﴿And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me﴾ [al-Baqarah 186] — what is meant there? It is du'a' of petition. And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too arrogant to worship Me will enter Hell in humiliation"﴾ [Ghafir 60] is du'a' of worship. Likewise the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error﴾ [al-Ra'd 14], meaning: their worship is only in error. Thus du'a' may mean du'a' of petition or du'a' of worship, so His saying "mā yad'ūn" includes both meanings; that is, what they worship and what they ask from it for their needs.

﴿Wa-anna mā yad'ūn﴾: as for his saying "bi-l-yā' wa-l-tā'" (with the yā' and the tā'), these are two recitations, both of the seven: ﴿wa-anna mā tad'ūn﴾ and ﴿wa-anna mā yad'ūn﴾, and both are correct. But in His saying ﴿wa-anna mā tad'ūn min dūnihi al-bāṭil﴾ there is address, and it can only be addressed to the disbelievers, because address of this kind cannot be directed to the Messenger ﷺ or to the believers among his Companions.

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Du'a' of petition.
* Student: Du'a' of petition, (...) du'a' of worship.
* Shaykh: He says: ﴿And that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood﴾. "Min dūnihi" means: from other than Him.

The author's saying "(they worship)" (...) this is deficient, and the correct wording is: they worship and they ask, as the Exalted said: ﴿And who is more astray than one who invokes other than Allah, those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Ahqaf 5]. "Yad'ū" here means "yas'al" (asks) ﴿other than Allah, those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection﴾. So here it should be added: they worship and they ask.

His saying "min dūnihi" means: from other than Him.

His saying "al-bāṭil": the author says "(al-zā'il)" (that which passes away), and this is open to scrutiny, because the intended meaning is falsehood, i.e., that which contains no good. From this is the hadith: "The truest word a poet has ever spoken is the word of Labid: 'Surely everything other than Allah is vain (bāṭil)'" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3841) and Muslim (2256/2) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. "Bāṭil" means: it contains no good.

His saying: ﴿And that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood﴾: is the intended meaning the falsehood of their worshipping it, or falsehood even in itself, such that it does not deserve worship?

Both matters are intended: it is falsehood with respect to their worshipping it, and it is falsehood in itself, deserving no share of divinity whatsoever.

(﴿And that Allah is the Most High﴾ over His creation by subjugation ﴿the Most Great﴾, the Magnificent.)

﴿And that Allah is the Most High﴾: this sentence, as you see, is a declarative sentence emphasized by the pronoun of separation (ḍamīr al-faṣl). Where is the pronoun of separation?

* Students: ﴿Huwa﴾.
* Shaykh: ﴿Huwa al-'Aliyy﴾, meaning: not other than Him.

And al-'Aliyy is an attributive adjective (ṣifah mushabbahah), because it is on the pattern (fa'īl), and the scholars of the Arabic language say that the attributive adjective indicates establishment and continuity (...).

* * *

﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour﴾ [Luqman 34]. It is well known that "Allah," the word of majesty, is the subject of (inna), "'indahu" (with Him) is the predicate preceding, and "'ilmu" (knowledge) is the delayed subject, and the clause is the predicate of (inna). A declarative clause contains restriction (ḥaṣr), and this is derived from the fronting of the predicate: the fronting of ﴿'indahu﴾, ﴿Indeed Allah, with Him﴾ and not with other than Him ﴿is the knowledge of the Hour﴾. This restriction is confirmed by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its arrival? Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord"﴾ [al-A'raf 187], restricted by the form ﴿innama﴾ (only): ﴿Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾. If someone claimed that the restriction here is in the predicate and not in the whole clause, we would say: the predicate is what indicated the restriction of the knowledge of the Hour to Allah, the Exalted, and what indicates and confirms it is the verse we mentioned: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its arrival? Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord"﴾. If such an expression reaches you, ﴿Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾, the meaning is: none knows it but my Lord; this is its meaning, just as when you say: "Only Zayd is standing," meaning: there is no one standing except Zayd.

His saying: ﴿'indahu 'ilmu al-sā'ah﴾ (with Him is knowledge of the Hour): when it will occur, and at what time, and none knows it but Allah. For this reason Jibril asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying: "Tell me about the Hour." He said: "The one asked about it knows no more than the one asking." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (50) and Muslim (9/5) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. Consider this: two messengers, one of them the best of the angels and the other the best of mankind, both say: "I have no knowledge," because his saying: "The one asked knows no more than the one asking" means: if you do not know, then I, by greater right, do not know. Therefore, knowledge of it is specific to Allah.

Whoever claims that he knows it has lied, especially by the means he mentioned as indicating it, as was published about a person called Rashad Khalifah. He is a man in America, a man who possesses knowledge, but he was greatly deceived by what he calls the number nineteen, claiming that the whole Qur'an is structured upon nineteen letters, and that this material he has, the nineteen, he used as evidence that he knows when the Hour will be established; he set it, I think, at a few years beyond 2000.

* Student: (...) the year 1909.
* Shaykh: 1909? 
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: 1909, how?
* Student: I mean: the year 1909 Hijri.
* Shaykh: Hijri, good. In reality, Allah knows best whether this man was a mistaken interpreter or a stubborn opponent, but whoever claims knowledge of the Hour is a disbeliever, because he denies Allah and His Messenger and the consensus of the Muslims, and the Muslims are in definitive consensus that none knows when the Hour will be established except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour﴾: the Hour is the Resurrection. It is called the Hour (al-sā'ah) because it is the greatest event that will occur, and because in it there is a warning to the deniers; for this reason one is threatened with "the Hour." One says, for example: "Your hour is with me." If you wish to threaten a person, you threaten him with the word "the Hour," because a great event will befall in it.

Second: ﴿And He sends down the rain﴾ [Luqman 34]. He did not say "and He knows when the rain will fall"; He said "and He sends down," and the difference of expression has a great meaning. Otherwise, all five of these are from the knowledge of the unseen, for the Prophet ﷺ explained the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen﴾ [al-An'am 59] with these five. The wording of the hadith is: "And none knows when the rain will fall except Allah." But the Qur'an says, in Allah's words: ﴿And He sends down the rain﴾, so how can we say that what is meant is: none knows when the rain will fall except Allah? We say: because Allah is the One who sends down the rain, none knows it except Allah, for He is the one who sends it down, and the one who sends down a thing is the one who knows it, while others do not know it.

His saying: ﴿al-ghayth﴾ [Luqman 34]: meaning the rain. It is called ghayth because by it hardship is removed, and istighathah (seeking relief) is the request for the removal of hardship; by rain the calamities are removed, the calamities of drought and the calamities of barrenness, so that people have water and have farms.

﴿And He knows what is in the wombs﴾ [Luqman 34]: "yaʿlamu mā" means: that which is in the wombs. He used "mā" because it is more general and comprehensive than "man" (who), since "man" is specific to what? To the rational being. This is one aspect. Another aspect is that "mā" is specific to attributes, while "man" is specific to essences. Have you not seen His saying: ﴿Then marry what seems good to you of women﴾ [al-Nisa' 3]? He did not say "man ṭāba" (whoever is good), even though the one married is a rational being, or not? Rather He said: ﴿mā ṭāba﴾, not "man," because marriage rests upon the attribute of the woman, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "A woman is married for four [things]" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5090) and Muslim (1466/53) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him]. Here He said "mā" rather than "man," because knowledge of what is in the wombs in terms of attributes is more eloquent than knowledge of it in terms of essence, more eloquent than knowledge of it in terms of being male or female. The fetus in the womb is not known merely by being male or female, or tall or short, or small or large; no, there is something more significant than that, which is the attributes of this fetus: will it be wretched or happy, long-lived or short-lived? Will its deeds be righteous or corrupt? For this reason the expression came with "mā," in which what is taken into account? The attributes are taken into account, because knowledge of what is in the wombs from this standpoint is greater than knowing whether it is male or female. Therefore, today they become aware of its knowledge of being male or female; they know this before it is born, whether male or female. Thus the eloquence of the Qur'an becomes clear in that it expressed with "mā" rather than "man," because "man" specifies the person, the identity of a rational being, whereas if it is non-rational one says "mā." As for what relates to attributes (...).

The adjective al-mushabbahah, the scholars of the Arabic language say, indicates establishment and continuity, and "al-'Aliyy" means High in His essence and High in His attributes; His highness is intrinsic and permanent, whether He is High in His essence or High in His attributes.

As for His saying: ﴿He is the Most High﴾ [Luqman 30]: it has already been mentioned to us that among the people of innovation are those who deny highness, which highness? The intrinsic highness. As for the highness of meaning (exaltation of status), it is agreed upon among the Muslims.

As for His saying: ﴿al-Kabir﴾ [Luqman 30], the author said: "(the Great)." He, glorified and exalted, is Great in the sense of magnificent in His essence and in His attributes: ﴿His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah 255]. Allah informed that the heavens will be folded up in His right hand, and that the earth entire will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and that He will fold up the heaven like the folding of a scroll for writings. All of this indicates the greatness of His essence, glorified and exalted, just as He is magnificent in His attributes.

* Student: His saying: ﴿jamī'an﴾ does it not indicate (...) ﴿and the earth entirely﴾ [al-Zumar 67]?
* Shaykh: No, it does not indicate that; it indicates the whole of the earth, but it does not indicate a number.
* Student: His saying: ﴿jamī'an﴾.
* Shaykh: Yes, the entire earth, including the trees, as came in the hadith: "He places the trees on one finger and the moist earth on one finger" [al-Bukhari (4811) and Muslim (2786/19) on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A rabbi came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, we find that Allah places the heavens on one finger, the earths on one finger, the trees on one finger, the water and the moist earth on one finger, and all other creatures on one finger, then He says, 'I am the King.'" The Prophet ﷺ laughed until his molars showed, confirming the rabbi's statement. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure; the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate﴾ [al-Zumar 67].]

Here, when He mentioned that Allah is the Truth, and that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, He said: ﴿And that Allah is the Most High, the Most Great﴾ [Luqman 30]. Because of His highness and His majesty, blessed and exalted is He, it becomes clear that these idols are the opposite of that: they are lowly, having no highness in them, they are humiliated and insignificant, having nothing of greatness.

* Student: The explanation of al-'Aliyy (...).
* Shaykh: No, His saying: "al-'Aliyy over His creation" here by subjugation. Yes. Rather, the correct view is that He is High in His essence and His attributes.

(﴿Have you not seen that the ships﴾ are ships ﴿sail through the sea by the favor of Allah, that He may show you of His signs? Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful one﴾ [Luqman 31] — ﴿'ibar﴾ lessons — ﴿for everyone patient﴾ in refraining from the disobedience of Allah, ﴿grateful﴾ for His blessings.)

﴿Have you not seen that the ships﴾: this interrogative is for affirmation (taqrir), because this is a matter that is seen, so one is not asked about its establishment, but its establishment is affirmed. And the address in His saying ﴿tara﴾ (you see) returns to whom? Either to the Messenger ﷺ, or to everyone who is fit to be addressed; and this is more general.

As for His saying: ﴿that the ships﴾, the author said: "(the ships)," so he took it as plural, although it may be intended as singular, by His saying ﴿tajrī﴾ (sails), and "al-fulk," as has already been mentioned, is a word used for both the plural and the singular. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Until when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind﴾ [Yunus 22]. Is "al-fulk" here singular or plural? Plural: ﴿until when you are in the ships and they sail﴾, ﴿wa-jarayna﴾ is not singular, it is plural; He did not say "wa-jarat." But here ﴿anna al-fulka tajrī﴾, the apparent meaning of the noble verse is that the singular is intended, since He did not say "yajrīna." Nevertheless, the singular may be intended to mean the plural in terms of meaning, because al-fulk is not one individual in number, but it is one in kind; as for individuals, they cannot be counted.

As for His saying: ﴿tajrī fī al-baḥr﴾ (sails in the sea), "fī" denotes location (lil-ẓarfiyyah). Is it on its original sense, or does it mean "'alā" (upon)?

* Students: It means "'alā" (upon).
* Shaykh: Is it on the sea or in it?
* Student: The submarine is in the sea.
* Shaykh: Yes, the submarine, is it?
* Student: It is a ship.
* Shaykh: But the ships that carry these cattle on their surface, yet in reality it is (...), not covering it, but its underside is covered by the water.

﴿fī al-baḥr bi-ni'mati Allāh﴾: the "bi" is connected to ﴿tajrī﴾; meaning: they sail with blessings, that is, carrying blessings. And it may be that the "bi" denotes causation, that is: they sail because of the blessing of Allah, meaning that Allah has blessed His servants with their sailing, and there is a difference between the two meanings, is there not? Yes; because on the first meaning the ships are carrying blessings, and on the second meaning the ships sail by the blessing of Allah, meaning that their sailing is among the favors of Allah upon us. The verse admits both meanings without contradiction, and we have mentioned again and again that when a verse admits two meanings without contradiction, both meanings are taken.

* Student: If there is a difference, but the apparent meaning is the latter; do we say (...) the first?
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: But their sailing by the blessing of Allah carries the cattle..

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 31, verse 30–34 (part 2 of 5):

* The Shaykh: No; because it may run empty, with nothing in it. It is merely God, Mighty and Majestic, enabling these ships to run upon the water, and water, as you know, is not a solid body that bears weight; rather it is a soft body. Were it not that God, exalted is He, made it easy for these ships to move upon it, they would not move.
* A student: Sometimes they sink into the water.
* The Shaykh: Yes. If they are carrying only passengers, they are in the first sense, by God's bounty. Usually there is in them a great deal of God's provision, so they are in the second sense. We say: they are in both senses together. They run by the grace of God, meaning by God's favour upon us, that their running is one of His blessings; and they run "with blessing," meaning carrying the blessing of God.

﴿لِيُرِيَكُمْ مِنْ آيَاتِهِ﴾ ("so that He may show you of His signs"): the lam is connected to ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ ("run") and is the lam of purpose, meaning: in order that He may show you. The meaning of (يُرِيَكُم) is that He makes it manifest so that you see it, that is: so that you may see of God's signs what overwhelms your minds.

Regarding His words ﴿لِيُرِيَكُمْ مِنْ آيَاتِهِ﴾ ("of His signs"): (مِن) here is partitive, since the ships and those riding on them do not see all of God's signs, but see only some of them.

His words ﴿لِيُرِيَكُمْ مِنْ آيَاتِهِ﴾ mean: of that which indicates His perfection in power and bounty, and other things. The word (الآيات) is the plural of (آية), which linguistically means a sign, and what is intended by it is everything by which one may infer the perfection of God, Mighty and Majestic, in His essence and attributes. What are the signs that are seen in the sea?
* A student: (...) the ships.
* The Shaykh: Such as?
* The student: The ships themselves float; and what is in it, for example, of very many animals of different colours and shapes, all of which are signs and indications of the power of God, glorified and exalted, just as on land there is the sea.
* The Shaykh: Correct, these are among the signs: what is in the sea of fish and great varied whales. Likewise, among His signs is what is witnessed in the sea in its waves, their strength and their calm; and likewise what is witnessed from the sea of vapours that rise and form clouds by the permission of God, Mighty and Majestic.
The important point is that these great signs are not all the signs, but they are among God's signs, some of His signs.

﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ﴾ ("Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful"): ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾, the referent of "that" is what was mentioned about the running of the ships in the sea by God's blessings, and what is witnessed in the sea of God's signs.
